name: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 3
aliases: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine due to SCN1A mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) Criteria for Familial Hemiplegic Migraine

criteria.description: At least one first- or second-degree relative with hemiplegic migraine
Recurrent attacks of unilateral motor weakness (hemiplegia) lasting minutes to days
Headache fulfilling migraine criteria with aura, temporally associated with hemiplegia
Identification of pathogenic SCN1A mutation associated with FHM3
Exclusion of other causes of hemiplegia such as stroke or epilepsy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent hemiplegic migraine attacks with family history and migraine headache fulfilling ICHD-3 criteria
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SCN1A mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically reversible motor weakness affecting one side of the body
Headache often preceded or accompanied by visual or sensory aura
Pathogenic variants in SCN1A gene causing neuronal sodium channel dysfunction
searchTerms: mutation in SCN1A gene causing seizures

common.notes: Transient sensory symptoms often accompanying hemiplegia

occasional.notes: Impaired coordination during or after attacks
Transient cognitive impairment during severe attacks

rare.notes: Occasional epileptic seizures reported in some patients
Rare severe attacks may cause prolonged unconsciousness

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal during attacks
imaging: Brain MRI usually normal between attacks
Transient cortical edema or diffusion abnormalities during severe attacks
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in SCN1A gene identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) may show nonspecific slowing during attacks

distinguishingFeatures: Similar clinical presentation but sporadic occurrence
Sudden onset neurological deficits without migraine headache
Postictal Todd’s paresis rather than migraine aura

redFlags: Persistent neurological deficits beyond typical attack duration
Signs of stroke or intracranial hemorrhage on imaging
references: Ophoff RA, Terwindt GM, Vergouwe MN, et al. Familial hemiplegic migraine and episodic ataxia type-2 are caused by mutations in the Ca2+ channel gene CACNL1A4. Cell. 1996.
Dichgans M, Freilinger T, Eckstein G, et al. Mutation in the neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel SCN1A in familial hemiplegic migraine. Lancet. 2005.
International Headache Society. The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3). Cephalalgia. 2018.
